source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះក្រូចថ្លុងដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ / Climate Resilience Pomelo Growing Technique", Nov 2018, 17pp
text:
Planting holes (ការរៀបចំដី និងការដាំដុះ) are dug roughly 1 x 1 meter and about 0.5 meter deep, sized to give young roots plenty of loosened soil to establish into. Compost or well-rotted manure is mixed into the topsoil used to backfill the hole, and a stake is set at planting time to support the young tree against wind while it establishes.

The seedling or hardened-off marcot is planted at the same depth it was growing in its nursery bag, the hole is backfilled and gently firmed, and the tree is watered immediately and regularly afterward to help roots establish into the surrounding soil.
